leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer B022 as a single three-person part (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer): a 2011 theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic angle followed by the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states, reproduced across many laboratories. All four word the citation around the prediction and the observed phases, not the pairing mechanism, and all four list B012 as an alternative. They differ on the second alternative (B027 for Danielsson, B018 for Eriksson, B056 for Mehlig, B013 for Pearce), on how much weight the field's youth deserves, and on how far the theory side can be described as predicting the correlated phases, which Eriksson cautions against. Pearce moved to B022 from an opening first place for B013. Experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero (Dean's group, the first author of the 2018 papers, Young, Yacoby, Efetov, Yazdani) is flagged as a concern by all four.

Four members prefer B012 as a single two-person part (Katori, Ye): the magic-wavelength lattice clock and its demonstration at about 10^-18, independently confirmed in several laboratories, with the 2005 frequency-comb prize regarded as not covering this step. All four rank it with B022 or B018 as alternatives (B022 for Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson, B038 then B022 for Johansson). They agree it has the cleanest attribution but concede that ion clocks, SYRTE, PTB, NIST and other lattice-clock groups are outside the pair, and that the SI redefinition of the second is pending. They differ on how much that redefinition matters (supporting evidence for Kroll and Lindroth, a possible reason to wait for Johansson) and on how the citation should be worded: around the lattice-clock architecture rather than record numbers. Johansson moved to B012 from an opening first place for B038.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members prefer a single-part prize: four for B022 and four for B012. No member prefers a two-part configuration, and no member's preferred configuration includes any other ballot.

B022 and B012 are mutual alternatives for most members: all four B022 supporters list B012, and all four B012 supporters list B022, so the committee is effectively choosing between a young, broad theory-plus-experiment field and a mature, tightly attributed instrument discovery.

Every member who addresses the supplied credit accepts that the B022 phenomenology (flat bands, correlated insulators, superconducting domes) is reproduced independently; the open question is mechanism and attribution, not existence.

Every member who addresses B012 accepts that the 10^-18 performance is independently confirmed and that Katori and Ye are the natural two names, with the dispute limited to whether the broader clock community is unfairly excluded.

Members who comment on B018 (Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce) identify the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang as a serious attribution problem for the supplied three names, and note overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phases.

Members who comment on B038 (Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce) agree that its attribution is unresolved (duplicate Ekert spellings, Wiesner's earlier conjugate coding), and Johansson himself no longer presses it.
scientific_disputes: Whether a discovery that opened a new regime of quantum matter (B022) should outweigh a precision-measurement invention (B012). Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig weight new phenomena and breadth; Kroll, Olsson and Lindroth treat a measurement that changes what can be tested as a discovery of the same kind.

Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism and the debated nature of several correlated states in B022 are an interpretation question separate from the secure discovery (Danielsson, Mehlig, Pearce) or a sign that the physics is not settled enough for a citation (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth).

How far the theory credit in B022 extends: Eriksson cautions that the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gives flat bands but does not predict the correlated phases, and Mehlig acknowledges that other theory groups worked on flat bands and moire structures.

Whether B012 is an incremental refinement after the 2005 frequency-comb prize or a distinct step: Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson say it is distinct; Danielsson and Mehlig, who rank it eighth, give it less conceptual reach.

Whether B013 (IceCube) should still be considered: Pearce no longer prefers it, Olsson notes that the diffuse flux is firm but source identification rests on a few modest associations, and Eriksson sees a collaboration-scale credit problem.
attribution_disputes: B022 experimental credit: all four supporters flag that Cory Dean's hBN-encapsulated devices and the groups of Young, Yacoby, Efetov and Yazdani, along with the first author of the 2018 papers, are outside Jarillo-Herrero. Mehlig and Danielsson treat this as a limit of the three-person rule; Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson treat it as a reason to rank B022 below B012. Pearce asks that the author record of the first reports be examined before final votes.

B012 credit: Lindroth, Olsson, Johansson and Kroll accept that trapped-ion groups, SYRTE, PTB, NIST, JILA team members and Hall and Haensch are outside Katori and Ye. Johansson notes that priority for the magic-wavelength idea over contemporaneous proposals has not been verified. Kroll and Lindroth propose wording the citation around the lattice-clock architecture so that ion-clock and comb contributors are not implicitly demoted.

B018: the supplied names (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) omit the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe prediction that motivated Molenkamp's experiment; Eriksson notes that Zhang's death makes the theory side hard to restore within the supplied strings.
B038: the shortlist carries two spellings of Ekert, Lindroth credits only Bennett and Brassard while Johansson credits Ekert as well, and Wiesner's earlier conjugate coding is outside the names.

B056: Eriksson proposes Bloch, Cirac and Zoller, while Johansson, Kroll and Mehlig propose Bloch, Greiner and Zoller; Esslinger is credited on the ballot but in none of the proposed trios. Lindroth and Olsson cite this as a reason to hesitate over B056.
maturity_disputes: B022 is about eight years old. Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig and Pearce hold that reproduced phenomenology suffices; Johansson ranks it sixth for prematurity, and Kroll and Lindroth prefer to let the field mature, though Eriksson concedes that waiting would settle both interpretation and credit.

B012: the SI second has not been redefined. Kroll and Lindroth treat that as supporting evidence of impact, not a criterion; Johansson asks whether it needs to happen first; Mehlig lists pending societal impact as a reason for his low ranking.
B013: Olsson sees source identification as still partial, and Pearce lists partial identification and AMANDA and DUMAND credit as the reasons he moved away from his opening first place.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll: documented research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, a loose lineage connection to the JILA community around Jun Ye (B012), with no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye; he would also recuse on B054, which is not shortlisted.
Olsson: University of Tokyo and JSPS fellowships and long-running exchanges with Japanese universities, where Katori works (B012); no documented direct tie, and she would accept recusal guidance.
Lindroth: atomic-theory field proximity to optical-clock physics (B012), not a personal or institutional tie; she would flag collaborations if an attosecond or electron-ion collision part arose.

Johansson: director of the Chalmers quantum-computing programme WACQT, with Chalmers links to the 2025 laureates; he has not preferred circuit-QED or quantum-computing candidates and notes uncertainty about his own bias toward quantum information.

Pearce (chair): membership in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur gives field proximity to B013, and more loosely to B027 and B008, with no documented tie to any credited individual and none to B022.

Danielsson and Eriksson: Danielsson flags a disciplinary preference for black-hole theory behind his B027 alternative; Eriksson flags methodological closeness to the band-structure side of B022; neither documents a personal or institutional link. Mehlig reports no conflict.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee verify the author and credit record of the 2018 B022 papers (including Dean's group and the first author) well enough to say whether Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero is an acceptable three-name allocation, and if not, whether the credit problem is large enough to move B022 below B012?

Should a B022 citation be restricted to the prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, with no claim about the pairing mechanism or about theory predicting the correlated phases?
Is eight years enough maturity for B022 given the unresolved superconducting mechanism and sample variability, or does that weight favour B012, which has been independently confirmed for years?

Is a precision-measurement invention (B012) a prize-level discovery of the same kind as a new regime of quantum matter (B022), and does cleaner attribution weigh more than breadth of impact when the two conflict?

Can a B012 citation be worded around the lattice-clock architecture and its 10^-18 realisation so that trapped-ion, comb and other lattice-clock contributors are not implicitly excluded, and has priority for the magic-wavelength proposal over contemporaneous proposals been checked?
Does the pending SI redefinition of the second count as supporting evidence of impact, a reason to wait, or neither?

Is there any fair two-part configuration that combines B022 and B012 within the three-person limit, given Pearce's report that he has found no split fair to both sets of credited names, or is the committee choosing one single part?

Can B018, B038 or B056 be repaired within the supplied credit (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, the Ekert duplicate and Wiesner, Cirac and Esslinger) to enter the comparison, or should they be set aside for this year?
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 files split four to four between two single-part configurations, B022 and B012, and each group names the other as its principal alternative. B022 has broader opening support and a theory-to-experiment narrative but carries open questions on maturity and experimental credit; B012 has the cleaner two-name attribution and settled confirmation but is an instrument-level result with a pending redefinition and credit that excludes ion-clock and other groups. Members in each camp say they would accept the other if the specific credit or maturity concern were resolved. B018, B038 and B056 are each set aside by their own proponents or critics because of unresolved attribution, and B013 is no longer a preferred position.
